The National Youth Service Corps says it has paid the delayed October 2026 allowance to corps members who served in Oyo State and completed their service year on October 29. The scheme attributed the delay to a technical glitch in the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System, the Federal Government platform used to process corps members’ monthly allowances. In a statement on Tuesday, the NYSC management said the affected corps members had been paid as of November 17, adding that anyone yet to receive the money by the close of business on Wednesday should contact the Oyo State Coordinator for verification. The statement was signed by the Director of Information and Public Relations, Caroline Embu. The management apologised for the delay, acknowledging that the affected corps members’ complaints were justified and that the situation might have caused them hardship. It explained that while other corps members received their October allowances before completing their service, payments to those in Oyo State were delayed by the technical problem with the GIFMIS platform. The NYSC, however, maintained that the allowance had been fully provided for in the budget and that no corps member’s entitlement had been withheld, diverted or reduced. It added that the allowances were paid directly into individual bank accounts from the scheme’s Central Bank of Nigeria account through the GIFMIS platform. It also disclosed that the Director-General of the NYSC, Brigadier General Olakunle Nafiu, met some of the affected corps members during his visit to the Oyo State Orientation Camp in Iseyin on Saturday, November 14. The management said Nafiu had assured them that the payment issue would be resolved. The statement read, “As expected, the affected Corps Members were sensitised by the Oyo State Coordinator on the cause of the delay in their payment. “Also, on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the Director-General, Brigadier General Olakunle Nafiu, met some of the affected Corps Members in person during his visit to the Oyo State Orientation Camp in Iseyin. “In line with the Director-General’s assurance, as of today, 17 November 2026, the affected Corps Members have been paid, and any of them not credited by close of business tomorrow, 18 November 2026, should notify the Oyo State Coordinator for necessary verification.” The development followed complaints by corps members who served in Oyo State that they had yet to receive their October allowance after completing their service year. The complaints attracted public attention, with some affected members taking to social media to demand payment of their entitlements. The NYSC management said it recognised the financial importance of the monthly allowance to corps members, particularly those posted to states where they had no family or established support networks. It described prompt payment of their allowances as an obligation rather than a favour. “Management appreciates the fact that Corps Members leave their homes to serve in States where many know no one, and that their allowance sustains them throughout the service year. “For this reason, it regards prompt payment of allowance to these patriotic Nigerians as a duty, not a favour,” the statement added. The management thanked the affected corps members for their patience and members of the public who drew attention to the delay. It also urged Nigerians to rely on the scheme’s official communication channels for clarification and avoid spreading unsubstantiated claims. The NYSC, established in 1973, is a mandatory one-year national service programme for eligible Nigerian graduates, with participants deployed to states outside their states of origin to promote national unity and development.
